patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 7's actuation step now states only that pressurized-fluid actuation moves the piston toward locked and explicitly disclaims chamber routing. The patent expressly describes actuation by a pressurized-fluid source and pneumatic motion in one embodiment (7d7e3f...). Master/tool units, piston, rollers, race, seal, and retarding behavior are supported by cited passages. FLUID is clearly qualified as an abstract boundary model element, not a patent-specified source architecture.

functional_completeness.rationale: The model captures the primary coupled units, piston/stem, retained rollers, tool locking race, piston/roller retarding mechanism, and separate stem-step/O-ring retardation variant. Omission of unsubstantiated robot/control interfaces and explicit actuator hardware is appropriate.

flow_consistency.rationale: Pressure boundary flow is directed from FLUID_OUT to PISTON_FLUID with compatible fluid types, and mechanical contact flows connect compatible inout ports. The fluid interface is an abstraction of the patent's pressurized-fluid actuation, not a claimed chamber path. No unsupported internal fluid route is asserted.

claim_traceability.rationale: Locking and retardation behavior and distinct O-ring restraint are supported; alternative ridge/conical geometries are described as alternatives. No unsupported engineering requirements are included.

interfaces.rationale: Connected interface records reference existing subsystems, ports and flows; both ends of the abstract fluid connection are represented reciprocally. Contact interface endpoints likewise match port types.

textbook_application.rationale: Physical components are modeled separately from actions, and an external context element is qualified as boundary abstraction, consistent with textbook guidance to represent context boundary exchanges without inventing internal structure.

summary: Independent review of saved revision 7 finds that the revised actuation wording resolves the prior concern: it no longer associates pressurized-fluid input with a particular chamber route, while accurately reflecting the patent's description of fluid actuation. The abstract external fluid context/interface is explicitly qualified and does not imply patent-specified supply topology. The complete model has grounded components and behaviors, coherent compatible interfaces and flow directions, traceable evidence, and no additional actionable issues identified. Textbook guidance is used only for modeling approach.
